title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 66
paragraphs: In the earlier war, then, as I said, they struggled against the Tegeans continually with ill success; but in the time of Croesus, and in the reigns of Anaxandrides and Ariston at Lacedaemon, the Spartans had at last become victors in the war. And they became victors in the following manner: since they kept being defeated by the men of Tegea, they sent messengers to consult the Oracle at Delphi and asked what god they should propitiate in order to prevail over the men of Tegea in the war. The Pythian prophetess answered them that they should bring into their land the bones of Orestes, son of Agamemnon. But as they were not able to find the grave of Orestes, they sent men again to go to the god and ask about the place where Orestes lay. When the messengers who were sent asked this, the prophetess said as follows:

“There is a place, Tegea, in Arcadian land, founded on a smooth plain, where two blasts blow by strong compulsion together; there is stroke and counter-stroke, and trouble upon trouble. There Agamemnon’s son lies resting in the life-giving earth; bring him home with you and you shall be master of Tegea.”

When the Lacedaemonians had heard this, they were no nearer finding it out, though they searched everywhere, until the time when Lichas, one of those Spartans called “Well-doers,” discovered it. Now the “Well-doers” are the oldest of the citizens who are passing out of the ranks of the “Horsemen,” five in each year; and these men are bound, during the year in which they leave the “Horsemen,” to allow themselves to be sent without ceasing to various places by the Spartan State.
